chunks: 3294 - And it was narrated from Ṭalḥah ibn Zayd, from al-Ṣādiq Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said:
"The testimony of children is valid among them so long as they have not dispersed or returned to their families."

key_terms.الصِّبْيَانِ: children; minors giving testimony about matters among themselves
key_terms.بَيْنَهُمْ: among them; within their own group or circle
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ: testimony or witness statement in a legal context
key_terms.يَتَفَرَّقُوا: they disperse or separate from one another

ai.seo_question: When is the testimony of children accepted in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling regarding the acceptance of the testimony of children in matters occurring among them. Its significance is that such testimony is considered valid only before they disperse or return to their families, indicating a specific evidentiary condition in judicial rulings.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3294 - And it was narrated from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), from his father Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), from his forefathers, from Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), who said:
"The testimony of children is valid among them as long as they have not dispersed or returned to their families."
